newsitem.title: ZIMBABWE: Zimbabwe opposition leader coup trial starts.
newsitem.headline: Zimbabwe opposition leader coup trial starts.

text.p: Veteran Zimbabwean opposition leader Ndabaningi Sithole goes on trial in Harare on Monday on charges of plotting to assassinate President Robert Mugabe and overthrow his government.
The 77-year-old president of the small ZANU-Ndonga party, an old rival of Mugabe, will be tried on charges that he controlled a shadowy group of rebels who he trained for sabotage work.

Sithole, arrested in October 1994 and detained for two days before being released, is alleged to have sent the group into neighbouring Mozambique for training as part of a conspiracy to murder and conduct acts of sabotage and "terrorism".
Sithole, a member of parliament who has been out on bail, denies the charges. He in turn has accused Mugabe of fabricating allegations to settle old personal scores.
Sithole believes Mugabe wants to destroy his political party, the only opposition group with seats in a parliament where Mugabe's ruling ZANU-PF controls 147 of the 150 seats.
The two men have been rivals since 1963 when they vied for the presidency of ZANU-PF at its formation, with Sithole winning it and Mugabe becoming secretary-general.

The rivalry worsened in the mid-1970s when Mugabe took over the party after accusing Sithole of abandoning the struggle and selling out to whites during the ZANU-PF-led guerrilla war against then white-ruled Rhodesia.
Mugabe assumed state power in Zimbabwe in 1980, and Sithole fled to the United States into self-imposed exile four years later over fears that Mugabe's government wanted to kill him.
At the time, the government denied the charge and accused Sithole of plotting to overthrow it.
He returned home in 1992 and the government alleges Sithole resumed his efforts to unseat Mugabe.

Two men -- William Nhamakonha, found with a rifle and anti-personnel mines on a road regularly used by Mugabe's presidential motorcade in 1995, and Simba Mhlanga who confessed he was a rebel commander -- were sentenced to 15 and 12 years respectively last year.
They had pleaded guilty to "terrorism" and murder charges.
